prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

TEXT_E:
Conservative Party Manifesto 2015 — Summary (ideological framing preserved)

Our plan is to secure a better future for you and your family at every stage of life by sticking to a clear Conservative approach: a strong economy first; rewarding hard work; backing aspiration; protecting the vulnerable; and keeping our country safe.

Economy and tax
- Finish the job: eliminate the deficit, run a surplus and start paying down debt to keep taxes and mortgage rates low.
- No rises in VAT, Income Tax or National Insurance; raise the Personal Allowance to £12,500 and the 40p threshold to £50,000; new Tax‑Free Minimum Wage law.
- Crack down on tax evasion and aggressive avoidance; keep competitive business taxes and cut £10bn more red tape.
- Rebalance growth: build the Northern Powerhouse, devolve powers and business rates growth, and back elected metro mayors.
- Invest over £100bn in infrastructure: HS2/HS3, road upgrades, frozen commuter fares, universal broadband, better mobile and 5G.

Jobs, skills and business
- Create 2 million more jobs and achieve full employment.
- Deliver 3 million new apprenticeships; abolish long‑term youth unemployment with tougher Day One requirements and a time‑limited Youth Allowance.
- Support SMEs with a business rates review, Start Up Loans, prompt payment and a permanent Office of Tax Simplification.
- Invest in science, innovation and high‑value industries; boost the rural economy and champion British farming and fishing.

Fair welfare and family support
- Make work pay: lower the household benefit cap to £23,000; roll out Universal Credit; freeze working‑age benefits (with key exemptions).
- 30 hours of free childcare for working parents of 3–4 year‑olds; tax‑free childcare; back marriage with transferable allowances.

Controlled immigration
- Keep net migration to the tens of thousands by reforming EU welfare rules, enforcing exit checks, clamping down on illegal working and exploitation, introducing a Controlling Migration Fund, and requiring fluent English in public‑facing roles.

Education and opportunity
- Protect per‑pupil funding; zero tolerance of failure; tougher standards in literacy/numeracy; core academic GCSEs.
- Turn every failing/coasting school into an academy; open 500 new free schools; expand UTCs and Degree Apprenticeships.
- Lift the cap on university places; introduce postgraduate loans; maintain world‑class research.

NHS and social care
- Increase NHS spending every year; at least £8bn extra by 2020 to deliver a truly 7‑day NHS, same‑day GP appointments for over‑75s, named GPs, and digital access.
- Lead on cancer, mental health parity, dementia research; integrate health and social care; cap residential care costs.

Homes and ownership
- Double first‑time buyers; extend Help to Buy and introduce Help to Buy ISAs; build 200,000 Starter Homes at 20% discount for under‑40s.
- Extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; prioritise brownfield; protect the Green Belt.

Law, security and justice
- Finish police reform; strengthen victims’ rights with a Victims’ Law; tackle extremism with new powers; reform prisons to cut reoffending.
- Scrap the Human Rights Act and introduce a British Bill of Rights.

Energy and environment
- Keep bills down through competition, smart meters and efficiency; back new nuclear, gas and promising renewables; halt new subsidies for onshore wind; support least‑cost carbon cuts.
- Protect nature with a UK and Overseas Territories Blue Belt; strengthen flood defences; plant 11 million more trees.

Culture, society and the Union
- Free entry to national museums; freeze the BBC licence fee; back creative industries and school sport; expand National Citizen Service and offer three days’ paid volunteering.
- Protect pensioners: triple lock, single‑tier pension, pension freedoms, retain key benefits; raise the effective Inheritance Tax threshold on the family home to £1m.
- Strengthen the Union: English votes for English laws; implement new powers for Scotland and Wales; support a stable, prosperous Northern Ireland.

Europe and the world
- Renegotiate Britain’s EU relationship and hold an in‑out referendum by end‑2017; keep the pound; reclaim powers; complete major trade deals.
- Maintain strong Armed Forces, renew Trident, meet NATO commitments; uphold 0.7% aid to tackle poverty, conflict and disease.

This is a disciplined, long‑term Conservative plan to reward work, back aspiration, protect vital services, and keep Britain strong, secure and free.

TEXT_C:
Stronger for Scotland: The SNP vows to shake up an out‑of‑touch Westminster so it serves Scotland better. A vote SNP is a vote to make Scotland’s voice heard, for progressive politics, and to end austerity. The SNP will never put the Tories into power; if there’s an anti‑Tory majority, it will work with others to lock them out and press Labour to deliver real change. We believe in independence, but this election is about making Scotland stronger at Westminster.

Public finances and growth: Replace austerity with modest annual spending increases, while having borrowing and debt fall as a share of income. Invest in infrastructure, productivity and jobs; create a sovereign wealth/energy fund; seed‑fund the Scottish Business Development Bank. Ensure the better‑off contribute a little more (restore 50p top rate; tax bankers’ bonuses; bank levy; mansion tax; end non‑doms; tackle avoidance).

Better off with the SNP: Protect the NHS from privatisation and secure an extra £2bn for Scotland’s NHS by 2020‑21. Raise the minimum wage to £8.70 by 2020; expand Modern Apprenticeships to 30,000; widen EMA. Increase Carer’s Allowance to JSA level; raise Universal Credit work allowance; retain the pension triple lock with a £160 single‑tier pension and review the rise to state pension age 67. Cut household energy bills by funding ECO from general taxation and forcing pass‑through of wholesale price cuts. Scrap the Bedroom Tax; halt Universal Credit and PIP roll‑out and reverse the DLA→PIP change; overhaul sanctions and Work Capability Assessments; protect disability support; end exploitative zero‑hours contracts.

Jobs and investment: Boost capital spending; connect Scotland to HS2 from north and south; accelerate broadband/4G with a Universal Service Obligation; target 100,000 UK affordable homes per year; devolve and cut APD, consider a VAT cut for hospitality; expand export finance. Back creative industries with a fair BBC Scotland share (+£100m) and support for games; stabilise the Annual Investment Allowance; raise the Employment Allowance to £6,000. Shape immigration to Scotland’s needs, including restoring post‑study work visas. Ensure small firms are paid on time.

Energy, climate and environment: Lead on carbon reduction and climate justice. Expand offshore wind and grid upgrades; support onshore wind, hydro, CCS and heat; grow community energy; maintain a fracking moratorium. Oppose new nuclear and block Trident renewal, redirecting billions to services. Protect species and end the ivory trade.

Rebalancing the UK and rural fairness: Invest in northern infrastructure and city deals; create a Scottish Cities Fund; secure Scotland’s fair CAP convergence share; protect Royal Mail’s USO and public interest stake; deliver rural fuel fairness; devolve food levies; return Crown Estate seabed revenues to coastal communities.

Rights, democracy and privacy: Promote fair work and the living wage; mandate equal pay audits; strengthen maternity protections. Scrap the House of Lords; adopt STV; effective MP recall; votes at 16–17. Defend the Human Rights Act and ECHR; remove VAT on sanitary products; let charities campaign. Oppose mass surveillance; back targeted, overseen powers.

Security, foreign affairs and EU: Strengthen Scotland’s conventional defence footprint and shipbuilding; improve care for service personnel; appoint an LGBTI rights envoy. Ensure any military action is UN‑lawful and Parliament‑approved. Recognise Palestine. Keep the UK in the EU; oppose Brexit and require a “double majority” in any referendum; exempt the NHS/Scottish Water from TTIP.

Home Rule: Deliver Smith in full and go further to full fiscal responsibility. Prioritise devolution of employment, welfare, business taxes, National Insurance and equalities—without UK vetoes—retaining Barnett in transition.

Record and pledge: SNP government has strengthened the NHS, improved schools, cut crime with 1,000 extra police, frozen Council Tax and mitigated Tory welfare cuts. On May 7, vote SNP to make Scotland’s voice heard and deliver a fairer, more prosperous, anti‑austerity UK.

Judge whether TEXT_E or TEXT_C aligns more closely with this profile, taking into account that each foundation may be invoked in either direction.
